about: I'm a full-stack developer based in Alicante, Spain, currently working at NTT DATA. I build and maintain business tools for employees using Angular, Spring Boot and Java, and I also write technical documentation for our projects.

I like projects where the backend and the frontend are designed together, not separately. My most recent personal project, similart, is a real-time multiplayer drawing game built with Angular, Express and Socket.IO — the same stack that powers this site.

projects.title: Similart
projects.problem: I wanted to build a project with real-time features, image processing, and a game that is easy to explain but fun to build.
projects.role: I designed and built the whole project on my own, in five repos. Three of them are microservices I created from scratch. similart-gateway is the only entry point: it sends login requests to jp-back-auth and game requests (HTTP and WebSocket) to similart-back-room. similart-back-room is the game engine: it keeps the rooms in memory, sends every stroke to the other players in real time with Socket.IO, and decides the winner by comparing each drawing with the original image. jp-back-auth is my own login service (Google or guest). It creates RS256 JWT tokens, and the game engine checks them locally with the public key, without calling it on every request. I also use it in my other apps. jp-similart-api has the TypeScript types that the frontend and the backend share, so if the stroke format changes, the error appears when compiling. The last repo is the Angular app where people play.
projects.outcome: A real-time drawing game for 1 to 12 players: everyone draws the same image at the same time and sees the other drawings and their match percentage live. It has a voting phase with a real countdown, a brush and a paint bucket, undo/redo that stays in sync with the room, reconnection if your connection drops, and an admin panel for the images that takes the color palette from each image automatically. Every feature is tested with Playwright, with 8 to 12 players at the same time in the same room.
projects.cvBullet: Real-time multiplayer drawing game with % similarity score, for 1 to 12 players. Built with Angular, Express, Socket.IO and PostgreSQL.

projects.title: This portfolio
projects.problem: I wanted a portfolio that helps me get interviews, not just a website that looks nice. Most developer portfolios are not built with that goal.
projects.role: I planned everything before writing any code: I researched what recruiters really look at, and I wrote down every performance decision from day one.
projects.outcome: A 100% static website (Angular and JSON only, no backend or database), pre-rendered and hosted on GitHub Pages. It works as a technical roadmap I can share, with a clear reason behind every decision.

projects.title: CalisMap
projects.problem: Most workout apps are just a log of sets and reps. In calisthenics you don't only want more reps, you want to unlock harder skills step by step, and no app showed me that path clearly.
projects.role: I designed and built the whole project on my own, split into three repositories: the mobile app (Ionic and Angular), the backend for the catalog and the sync (Express and PostgreSQL, private repo) and the login. For the login I didn't build a new one: the app uses jp-back-auth, my own authentication microservice with Google and guest login, which I share between several of my apps (CalisMap, Mudanza and Similart). It gives a JWT signed with RS256 and each backend checks it with the public key, without calling the auth service on every request. The account button comes from jp-user-kit, a small UI library I publish on GitHub Packages so I can reuse it in other apps.
projects.outcome: A mobile app where every skill (Muscle Up, Planche, Handstand Push-up...) is a roadmap: each step unlocks the next one when you reach a level from Bronze to Diamond, calculated from your own marks. It works offline and without an account (your data is saved on the device first), syncs when you log in with Google, and can import your history from apps like Strong or Hevy. It also has an admin panel to manage the catalog. Deployed on GitHub Pages, Render and Neon.

projects.title: PayToWin
projects.problem: An academic project from my Web Application Development studies: an online video game store with users, a shopping cart, orders and invoices, built with Java and a real database.
projects.role: I built the whole application: the database design and scripts, the Java backend with Servlets and DAOs, and the JSP pages. Later, I fixed the security problems and deployed it with Docker.
projects.outcome: A working store with client and admin accounts: catalog, shopping cart, orders, invoices you can export to PDF and XML, product management with image upload, and sales statistics. Public demo on Render.
